identification.summary: Violet Typhoon is a China-based espionage actor. Microsoft says it has focused on espionage since 2015, targeting former government and military personnel, NGOs, think tanks, higher education, media, and the financial and health sectors in the United States, Europe and East Asia [S1]. Other vendors and governments track the same activity as APT31 and ZIRCONIUM [S1][S12]. US prosecutors allege that the APT31 operators worked through Wuhan Xiaoruizhi Science & Technology, a front company for the Hubei State Security Department of the Ministry of State Security (MSS) [S2][S3]. In July 2025 Microsoft named Violet Typhoon as one of the China-based actors exploiting on-premises SharePoint vulnerabilities [S1].
identification.firstObserved: Microsoft: dedicated to espionage since 2015 [S1]. The March 2024 US indictment alleges APT31 campaigns from at least 2010 [S2][S3]. Check Point reports that APT31 cloned an Equation Group exploit in 2014 and used it from about 2015 [S11].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Violet Typhoon (formerly ZIRCONIUM) [S10][S12]. Aliases stated in cited coverage include APT31, ZIRCONIUM, BRONZE VINEWOOD, JUDGMENT PANDA, Red Keres and TA412 [S12], and Altaire [S2]. MITRE tracks the group as ZIRCONIUM/APT31 (G0128) [S13]. Start dates differ by source: Microsoft says 2015 [S1], while DOJ alleges activity from 2010 [S2]. Government attributions (US, UK, Finland, Czechia) use the name APT31 and not Microsoft's name [S2][S4][S5][S7].

attribution.sponsor: People's Republic of China, Ministry of State Security (MSS). The US alleges operations ran through the Hubei State Security Department using the front company Wuhan Xiaoruizhi Science & Technology (Wuhan XRZ) [S2][S3].
attribution.confidence: In March 2024 the US Department of Justice unsealed charges against seven alleged APT31 members, and Treasury sanctioned Wuhan XRZ and two individuals [S2][S3]. The UK NCSC assessed that APT31 was 'almost certainly' responsible for reconnaissance of UK parliamentarians' email accounts in 2021 [S4]. Czech authorities attributed a campaign against the Foreign Ministry to APT31 with a 'high degree of certainty' and linked APT31 to the MSS in May 2025 [S7], and NATO issued a statement of solidarity [S14]. Finland's Supo attributed the 2020 Finnish Parliament intrusion to APT31 but did not name China [S5]. Microsoft describes Violet Typhoon as China-based [S1].
attribution.basis: US indictment and Treasury/UK sanctions [S2][S3][S4]; national attributions by Finland, France (ANSSI technical report), the UK and Czechia [S4][S5][S6][S7]; vendor telemetry and reporting from Microsoft, Google, Check Point and Positive Technologies [S1][S8][S9][S10][S11].

objectives: Political and strategic espionage for the PRC state. This includes surveillance of political dissidents and their supporters inside and outside China, collection on government officials, legislators and election campaigns, and access to companies and research institutions [S1][S2][S3][S4][S9][S10]. Reporting from 2025 shows collection against government IT contractors in Russia, which suggests the actor also collects on partner states [S8].

sectors: Government officials and legislators (US executive departments, Congress, UK and Finnish parliaments) [S2][S4][S5]
IT contractors and integrators serving government [S8]
regions: Europe, including the UK, Finland, France and Czechia [S1][S4][S5][S6][S7]
targeting.notes: ANSSI said it could not identify sector or thematic criteria in the 2021 French campaign and assessed it as opportunistic [S6]. The Russian IT-sector activity rests on Positive Technologies reporting, as covered by The Hacker News. The report does not name China [S8].

capabilities.summary: Large-scale reconnaissance phishing. More than 10,000 emails, often disguised as news articles, carried hidden tracking links that reported back recipient and network details. The actor then followed up with intrusions that included compromising home routers and other devices [S2][S3]. Microsoft observed ZIRCONIUM using web bugs (tracking URLs) against people tied to the 2020 US election [S10]. Google reported McAfee-themed phishing against Biden campaign staff. The lure delivered a Python implant hosted on GitHub that used Dropbox for command and control [S9]. Microsoft says Violet Typhoon persistently scans exposed web infrastructure and installs web shells, and in July 2025 it exploited on-premises SharePoint vulnerabilities [S1]. The actor has used anonymizing networks of hijacked SOHO routers managed by malware ANSSI calls Pakdoor [S6]. Check Point found that APT31 cloned the Equation Group 'EpMe' exploit for CVE-2017-0005 into a tool called 'Jian' [S11]. Positive Technologies reports cloud-service C2 through Yandex Cloud, OneDrive and Dropbox, with tools including CloudyLoader, OneDriveDoor, CloudSorcerer, COFFProxy, LocalPlugX, Cobalt Strike, Mimikatz and Tailscale [S8].

campaigns.name: Jian (cloned EpMe exploit)
campaigns.summary: Check Point reports that APT31 cloned the Equation Group EpMe exploit (CVE-2017-0005) and used it as 'Jian' until Microsoft patched it in March 2017. Lockheed Martin's IR team reported the in-the-wild exploit.

campaigns.name: Finnish Parliament intrusion
campaigns.summary: Parliamentary email accounts, including some belonging to MPs, were compromised. Supo publicly attributed the intrusion to APT31 on 2021-03-18.

campaigns.name: 2020 US election targeting
campaigns.summary: Microsoft reported ZIRCONIUM targeting people tied to the Biden campaign and international affairs leaders using web bugs. Google reported McAfee-lure phishing that delivered a GitHub-hosted Python implant with Dropbox C2.

campaigns.name: UK parliamentarian reconnaissance
campaigns.summary: The NCSC assessed that APT31 almost certainly conducted reconnaissance against UK MPs' and peers' email accounts. Parliament mitigated the campaign before any accounts were compromised.

campaigns.name: French campaign via hijacked routers
campaigns.summary: ANSSI reported a large APT31 campaign against French entities that used a mesh of compromised routers controlled by Pakdoor malware.

campaigns.name: Czech Foreign Ministry intrusion
campaigns.summary: Czechia attributed a campaign against an unclassified Foreign Ministry network, running since at least 2022, to APT31 on 2025-05-28.

campaigns.name: Russian IT contractor intrusions
campaigns.summary: Positive Technologies reports attacks between 2024 and 2025 with long dwell time in Russian government IT contractors, with C2 over Yandex Cloud and OneDrive and spear-phishing that delivered CloudyLoader in December 2024.

campaigns.name: US indictment and US/UK sanctions
campaigns.summary: DOJ charged seven alleged APT31 members, citing campaigns since 2010. OFAC and the UK sanctioned Wuhan XRZ, Zhao Guangzong and Ni Gaobin.

campaigns.name: SharePoint 'ToolShell' exploitation
campaigns.summary: Microsoft named Violet Typhoon, Linen Typhoon and Storm-2603 as exploiting on-premises SharePoint vulnerabilities, with exploitation attempts seen as early as 2025-07-07.

diamond.adversary: MSS Hubei State Security Department operators working through the front company Wuhan XRZ. Seven are named in the US indictment, including Ni Gaobin and Zhao Guangzong [S2][S3].
diamond.capability: Tracking-link reconnaissance email, web shells, exploitation of SharePoint and other web infrastructure, cloned exploits (Jian), Python and cloud-C2 implants, and the Pakdoor router botnet [S1][S2][S6][S8][S9][S11].
diamond.infrastructure: Hijacked SOHO routers used as anonymizing relays [S6]. Legitimate cloud services (GitHub, Dropbox, OneDrive, Yandex Cloud) are used for staging and C2 [S8][S9]. Actor-purchased domains host web bugs [S10].
diamond.victim: Legislators, government officials, foreign ministries, election campaigns, dissidents, NGOs, think tanks, academia, media, and government IT contractors [S1][S2][S4][S5][S7][S8][S10].
diamond.socioPolitical: PRC state collection on foreign political processes, policy-makers and critics of the CCP [S2][S3][S4].
diamond.technology: Email systems, internet-facing web and collaboration servers such as on-premises SharePoint, consumer and SOHO routers, and cloud storage platforms [S1][S2][S6][S8].

gaps: Primary documents could not be opened in this session: the DOJ indictment and press release, Treasury OFAC release, NCSC statement, CERT-FR CERTFR-2021-CTI-013, the NÚKIB statement, Check Point research, Google TAG blog and Microsoft's 2020 election blog. Details rely on secondary coverage or search-result text.
Start date conflict: Microsoft says 2015, DOJ alleges 2010, and Check Point places tool development in 2014. These differences are unresolved.
The Positive Technologies Russian IT report does not itself name China. The APT31 label there is the vendor's, and the original report was not reviewed.
The UK Electoral Commission breach (2021-2022) was attributed to a Chinese state-affiliated actor, not specifically to APT31. Do not merge it into this record.
Specific SharePoint CVEs, victims and post-exploitation activity attributable to Violet Typhoon in July 2025 are not broken out in the Microsoft blog.
Whether the 2020 ZIRCONIUM election activity counts of 'about 150 successes' is accurate could not be verified against Microsoft's original post.
The alias list comes from Microsoft-adjacent press coverage. A per-vendor mapping (Microsoft MicrosoftMapping.json) was not checked in this session.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1 (operational environment): Key terrain is the personal and official email of leaders and staff, internet-facing collaboration servers (SharePoint), SOHO and home routers of personnel, and IT contractors that support government networks [S1][S2][S6][S8]. STEP 2 (effects): Tracking-link reconnaissance can map who reads which messages and from which networks before any malware is delivered. Router botnets and cloud C2 blend with legitimate traffic and complicate IP-based blocking [S2][S6][S8][S9]. STEP 3 (threat model): The template is mass tracking email, then targeted phishing or exploitation of exposed web infrastructure, then a web shell or cloud-C2 implant, then long-dwell collection that is often timed for holidays and weekends [S1][S2][S8]. STEP 4 (COAs): MLCOA is persistent political and policy espionage against officials, legislators and partner-nation ministries, including senior leaders' personal accounts and home routers. MDCOA is rapid exploitation of a newly disclosed collaboration-server flaw across DoD-adjacent and contractor networks during a crisis to harvest planning data [S1][S7][S8]. Candidate indicators: emails with embedded remote-image or tracking URLs to newly registered domains [S2][S10]; new ASPX web shells on SharePoint servers [S1]; outbound traffic to Dropbox, OneDrive or Yandex Cloud from servers [S8][S9]; and inbound connections from residential router IP space [S6].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: fuse reporting on reconnaissance email and tracking beacons with collaboration-server patch status, because early beacons precede intrusion [S1][S2]. (2) Authorities: much of the targeted terrain (personal accounts, home routers, contractor networks) lies outside DODIN boundaries, so mitigation requires coordination with DC3/DIB CS, CISA and FBI rather than unilateral DoD action [S2][S6][S8]. (3) Mission assurance: protect senior leader and staff communications and planning collaboration platforms, and enforce rapid patching and machine-key rotation for SharePoint [S1]. (4) Coordination: APT31 activity against NATO allies (UK, Finland, France, Czechia) supports coalition indicator sharing through NATO and national CERTs [S4][S5][S6][S7][S14].

provenance.importedSummary: FireEye characterizes APT31 as an actor specialized on intellectual property theft, focusing on data and projects that make a particular organization competetive in its field. Based on available data (April 2016), FireEye assesses that APT31 conducts network operations at the behest of the Chinese Government. Also according to Crowdstrike, this adversary is suspected of continuing to target upstream providers (e.g., law firms and managed service providers) to support additional intrusions against high-profile assets. In 2018, CrowdStrike observed this adversary using spear-phishing, URL “web bugs” and scheduled tasks to automate credential harvesting.
